title: Node identity: AKS vs EKS vs GKE
summary: Every node carries a cloud identity for its own work, such as pulling images. Pods share the node, so each cloud needs some way to keep them away from it.

dimensions.label: How pods are kept away
values: GKE metadata server (comes with Workload Identity)

dimensions.label: Default to watch out for
values: Extra roles granted to the kubelet identity
Hop limit 2, IMDSv1, CNI policy on the node role
Compute Engine default SA with Editor

notes: Rule for all three: the node identity is infrastructure. Application permissions belong on per-service-account identities. See the 'App permissions on the node role' warning.
GKE is the only one where enabling workload identity also closes the node-credential path. On AKS and EKS it's a separate setting you must remember.
